text:
maria: quick q — we bumped a transitive dep in infra/registry lock; no behavior change. should this be a patch (x.y.Z) or do we stick buildmeta (+build.123) and not touch semver?
kevin: if it's deps-only and doesn't change runtime contracts i'd keep a patch bump. our release tooling treats semver bumps as the signal for release notes and rollback windows.
maria: ah — our packaging strips +buildmeta for artifact tags so buildmeta wouldn't show up in the release tag — is that still problematic for ops?
kevin: buildmeta is fine for internal artifacts but deploybot matches exact semver tags for targeted rollouts. if there's no semver bump it won't trigger the normal release flow.
irene: fwiw SRE prefers explicit patch bumps for lockfile-only updates so teams can pin to a known semver for fast rollback. buildmeta makes pinning fuzzy.
sam: +1 to patch. also helps changelog automation: only semver bumps become release-note candidates in our pipeline.
maria: ok leaning patch then. any objections from release engineering before i open the PR?
deploy-bot: deploy started for tag v2.14.3 -> candidate v2.14.4 at 2025-10-12T09:04:16Z — rollout 0% -> 30%
kevin: note — if we do a patch bump, please include a concise CHANGELOG entry like `deps: bump transitive xyz (no behavioral change)` and mark it `changelog: non-functional`. keeps audit clean.
irene: also flag dedicated customers — we sometimes hold lockfile-only bumps until their maintenance window unless requested.
maria: good call, i'll add `hold-for-dedicated` if needed and ping support after PR lands.
sam: if anything weird shows up during rollout we can `!rollback v2.14.3` — deploybot supports immediate rollback and will re-pin traffic.
deploy-bot: rollback command acknowledged if issued; current rollout at 30%, estimated completion 00:12:00.
maria: proceeding with patch PR now, will update this thread when merged and when rollout completes.
kevin: :thumbsup:
